original_question: If X is a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space, must there exist a sequence (X_n) of subspaces of X that are pairwise non-isomorphic?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 7 (G. Godefroy): whether every separable Banach space that is not Hilbertian contains countably many mutually non-isomorphic subspaces.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target very closely: it has the correct ambient object (a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space), the correct quantifier shape (existence of a sequence), and the correct conclusion (the subspaces should be pairwise non-isomorphic). It also stays on Problem 7 rather than drifting to the stronger neighboring Problem 8 about continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces under extra type/cotype hypotheses (Section 6, Problem 7; compare Problem 8, around pp. 440-441).
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone formulation, 'non-Hilbertian' should be unpacked as 'not isomorphic, as a Banach space, to a Hilbert space' (intended in Section 6, Problem 7, p. 440).

In the Banach-space terminology used here, 'subspace' should be made explicit as 'closed linear subspace'; Section 1 states that notation and terminology are standard Banach-space notation (Section 1, p. 435).

To avoid a trivial finite-dimensional reading, the subspaces should be stated to be infinite-dimensional. This is implicit from the surrounding context, since the authors first note as a nontrivial known fact that every separable non-Hilbertian Banach space contains two non-isomorphic subspaces before asking for a whole sequence (Section 6, paragraph immediately before Problem 7, p. 440).

The sequence should be explicitly understood as indexed by the natural numbers, i.e. a countably infinite family, because the paper asks for a sequence here, not merely 'infinitely many' and not the stronger 'continuum many' from Problem 8 (Section 6, Problem 7 versus Problem 8, pp. 440-441).
'Pairwise non-isomorphic' should be spelled out as: for m ≠ n, X_m is not isomorphic to X_n as Banach spaces (Section 6, Problem 7, p. 440).

No extra hypotheses such as reflexivity, basis assumptions, or type/cotype restrictions belong in this question; Problem 7 is stated without them, while Problem 8 is the nearby variant that adds type/cotype assumptions (Section 6, Problems 7-8, pp. 440-441).

The paper does not impose a special scalar field; it uses standard Banach-space conventions from the introduction, so no additional real/complex restriction should be inserted unless one wants to add it for exposition (Section 1, p. 435).
refined_question: Does every separable Banach space X that is not isomorphic to a Hilbert space contain a sequence (X_n) indexed by the natural numbers of closed infinite-dimensional subspaces of X such that, whenever m ≠ n, the Banach spaces X_m and X_n are not isomorphic?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 6, Problem 7, not the block-homogeneous-basis question itself (Problem 6) and not the stronger type/cotype variant (Problem 8). The refinement keeps exactly the same mathematical intent as Problem 7 and only makes explicit the Banach-space conventions that are implicit in the paper: 'non-Hilbertian' is meant in the isomorphic sense, 'subspace' is read in the Banach-space sense, and the subspaces should be taken infinite-dimensional so that the question is nontrivial in the sense indicated by the preceding sentence about the known existence of two non-isomorphic subspaces (Section 6, paragraph before Problem 7, p. 440). Section 1 supports this sharpening by stating that the paper uses standard Banach-space notation and terminology (Section 1, p. 435).
